hypotheses.title: 1. Preparation and maturation differences account for much of the apparent activity gap
hypotheses.question_and_explanation: Does pig ADA2 remain less active when equivalent amounts of properly processed, folded protein are compared? CTX-01 reports lower activity but provides no effect size or assay conditions. Different annotated signal peptides and glycosylation sites provide a reason to examine maturation, not proof of its involvement (CTX-03). The general biochemical hypothesis is that unequal functional protein amounts, glycosylation, processing, or zinc loading could produce an apparent species difference without different intrinsic catalytic chemistry.
hypotheses.evidence_notes: The constructs, protein quality, glycan occupancy, zinc occupancy, and assay conditions are not provided. No supplied observation directly demonstrates a preparation artifact. Predicted dimers do not establish that the experimental preparations are folded or dimeric.
hypotheses.alternative_explanation: An intrinsic sequence-dependent difference persists even in equivalently prepared human and pig ADA2.
hypotheses.proposed_test: First verify both construct sequences, including the actual minipig sequence. Compare independent human and pig preparations made in the same expression system with matched tag handling. Measure free-adenosine conversion over substrate concentrations under shared assay conditions, alongside protein amount, processing, glycosylation, folding, oligomeric state, and zinc occupancy. If a preparation feature differs, test whether correcting that feature rescues activity without changing sequence.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome_if_true: The activity gap substantially contracts after preparation matching, or pig activity changes reproducibly with correction of a specific maturation or loading difference.
hypotheses.falsifying_outcome: A reproducible activity gap persists across independent, well-characterized preparations with comparable protein amount, folding, processing, oligomeric state, and zinc loading under shared conditions.
hypotheses.controls_and_feasibility: Use human and pig wild-type proteins, independent preparation batches, no-enzyme controls, and product-recovery controls to detect assay interference. Compare glycan manipulations only with corresponding sham-treated samples and folding checks. Recombinant expression and characterization are supported by CTX-08; specific methods for glycan, metal, and oligomer analysis require confirmation with the team.
hypotheses.next_decision: If matching rescues activity, standardize the responsible preparation feature before interpreting species biology. If the gap persists, prioritize intrinsic sequence and substrate-selectivity tests. If protein quality remains unequal, resolve that uncertainty before mutagenesis.
hypotheses.added_value_from_computation: This experiment follows mainly from background records and general biochemical knowledge. STRUCT-02 makes a gross inability of the reference pig sequence to adopt a dimer less compelling, but cannot exclude defective folding or assembly in actual preparations. The glycan-free predictions cannot test the maturation explanation.

hypotheses.title: 2. Sequence differences near the predicted interior shifts alter catalytic coupling or dimer organization
hypotheses.question_and_explanation: Do the candidate sequence differences around human-aligned positions 281 and 347 contribute causally to lower free-adenosine activity? STRUCT-08 reports confident local structural shifts near V277A, E278K, E282G, K346S, and D347R. STRUCT-03 also predicts a modest difference in relative chain arrangement. As a general mechanistic possibility, these changes could influence substrate handling or coupling between subunits without destroying the overall fold; their proximity to functional sites has not been established.
hypotheses.evidence_notes: STRUCT-02 argues against gross predicted dimer disruption, not against subtle functional changes. The shifts are predictions, and neither catalytic effects nor a connection between these regions and the dimer interface has been measured. Residue correspondence remains dependent on a draft alignment.
hypotheses.alternative_explanation: The predicted differences are functionally neutral species variation; the activity gap instead arises from preparation differences or sequence changes elsewhere.
hypotheses.proposed_test: After validating the construct alignment, map these candidate regions relative to the catalytic site and interface. Test reciprocal human-to-pig and pig-to-human substitutions in the two regions separately, followed by individual substitutions if a regional change has an effect. Compare free-adenosine kinetics, folding, and oligomeric state. If activity changes without altered dimer abundance, a solution-structure comparison could distinguish altered dimer geometry from a local catalytic effect.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome_if_true: Humanizing at least one pig candidate region increases activity, while the reciprocal human change reduces it, without corresponding loss of protein integrity. A reproducible geometry or assembly change tracking activity would additionally support the dimer-coupling mechanism.
hypotheses.falsifying_outcome: Validated reciprocal changes leave activity unchanged in well-folded, equivalently prepared proteins. Activity changes explained entirely by altered protein recovery or denaturation would weaken the proposed specific catalytic-coupling mechanism.
hypotheses.controls_and_feasibility: Include both wild types, sham-engineered controls, matched expression and purification, equal protein amounts, and processing, glycosylation, zinc-loading, and folding checks. CTX-08 supports recombinant protein work broadly. A method capable of resolving a modest solution-state dimer geometry difference must be confirmed; oligomer abundance alone cannot establish geometry.
hypotheses.next_decision: If reciprocal activity effects occur, resolve the responsible substitutions and then distinguish local substrate handling from dimer coupling. If only protein stability changes, pursue a stability mechanism instead. If neither region affects activity, deprioritize these candidates rather than expanding mutagenesis solely from model confidence.
hypotheses.added_value_from_computation: STRUCT-08 supplies candidate regions for targeted experiments rather than an unguided species-wide swap. STRUCT-04 and STRUCT-05 reduce concern that the predicted differences arise solely from template use or seed variation. STRUCT-06 and STRUCT-07 discourage prioritizing the largest shifts near the insertion or chain ends, where alignment and confidence are weaker. No supplied calculation yet places the selected candidates at the active site or interface.

hypotheses.title: 3. Pig ADA2 has altered substrate preference while retaining DNA-associated activity
hypotheses.question_and_explanation: Is pig ADA2 selectively poor at using free adenosine rather than broadly catalytically inactive? CTX-04 reports ADA2–DNA interactions and deoxyadenosine-to-deoxyinosine conversion within DNA, motivating a test of whether pig ADA2 retains DNA binding and editing despite reduced free-adenosine activity. Substrate-dependent engagement or positioning is a general mechanistic hypothesis, not an observed pig property. Binding could also persist even if editing does not.
hypotheses.evidence_notes: No supplied record measures pig ADA2 binding or editing DNA. CTX-04 is a draft literature observation requiring verification. The similar predicted folds do not establish preservation of any DNA function, and the models contain no DNA.
hypotheses.alternative_explanation: Pig ADA2 has a general catalytic defect and retains, at most, noncatalytic DNA binding. Apparent DNA editing could instead reflect a copurifying enzyme, free nucleoside contamination, or DNA degradation.
hypotheses.proposed_test: Using matched, characterized preparations, compare free-adenosine conversion, free-deoxyadenosine conversion, DNA binding, DNA-associated deoxyinosine formation, and DNA integrity as separate readouts. Directly establish that the editing product originated within DNA rather than from free nucleosides. Compare the pig-to-human activity relationship across substrates; the free-deoxyadenosine arm separates sugar preference from a requirement for DNA context.
hypotheses.predicted_outcome_if_true: Pig ADA2 shows a smaller activity deficit on DNA-associated substrate than on free adenosine, together with measurable DNA binding and enzyme-dependent DNA editing. Preservation only on free deoxyadenosine would instead indicate nucleoside preference, not necessarily a DNA-context advantage.
hypotheses.falsifying_outcome: Pig loses DNA editing to the same extent as free-substrate activity under conditions where human ADA2 edits DNA. Binding without editing would contradict preserved DNA catalysis while supporting retention of a separate binding function. A signal attributable to free nucleosides or contaminants would not support the hypothesis.
hypotheses.controls_and_feasibility: Include human ADA2 as a positive comparator, no-protein and mock-purification controls, independent protein preparations, and separately validated controls for binding, product detection, and DNA cleavage. Match protein amount and assess folding, processing, glycosylation, assembly, zinc loading, and assay conditions. CTX-08 supports relevant broad expertise, but suitable DNA-editing measurements and analytical sensitivity must be confirmed. The existing ADA2 aptamer is not evidence of generic DNA binding or pig cross-reactivity.
hypotheses.next_decision: If pig DNA editing is relatively preserved, prioritize substrate-recognition mechanisms and then test cellular localization and DNA/TLR9 consequences separately. If only binding persists, pursue noncatalytic partner interactions without claiming editing. If neither persists, deprioritize conserved DNA functions under the tested conditions; this would not exclude other unknown functions.
hypotheses.added_value_from_computation: This hypothesis comes from CTX-01 and CTX-04 plus general substrate-specificity reasoning. The supplied structural predictions do not directly change the DNA experiment because they lack DNA and glycans and provide no DNA-binding analysis. CTX-07 motivates eventual cellular follow-up but does not identify which molecular function is preserved in pigs.

overall_note: Start by reproducing the activity difference with verified constructs and matched preparations: its magnitude and conditions are not provided, and the reference pig sequence may not match the experimental minipig construct. The computations prioritize candidate tests but establish neither catalytic impairment nor conserved DNA function. Binding, DNA editing, DNA cleavage, and cellular inflammatory effects require separate evidence.
